readers.summary: The CUDA attach pipeline (attach/nv_attach_impl, GPU maps, llvmbpf PTX output) was read end to end and partly tested on the Orin Nano (sm_87, CUDA 13.2). The GPU-side half works here: a replica of bpftime's PTX rewrite, compiled with nvPTXCompiler for sm_87, ran on the GPU with a host-memory map, and gave the expected results. Two problems block real use. (1) The build cannot find CUDA, because cmake/cuda.cmake looks in targets/aarch64-linux and CUDA 13.2 here only has targets/sbsa-linux; this is easy to fix. (2) Programs compiled with CUDA 13 start kernels through a new handle-based API (__cudaGetKernel/__cudaLaunchKernel). bpftime cannot match that handle to a kernel name, so no <<<>>> launch is sent to the patched module, and nothing reports it. Also, CUDA IPC memory handles are not supported on this iGPU, so the IPC-based GPU map types cannot be created; only the HOST map variants and ordinary maps work. Repo paths are relative to the candidate worktree; my test files are under /tmp/claude-2002/-home-jetson-src/6ac0883f-4479-466c-bec5-5fa31cffe4de/scratchpad/gpu-env/attach-probe.

findings.topic: Build paths
findings.detail: find_cuda() hard-codes targets/aarch64-linux for include and lib dirs, but /usr/local/cuda-13.2 has only targets/sbsa-linux. CMake configures fine, then compilation fails on missing CUDA headers. When given the correct include dir, all 25 CUDA-attach source files parse cleanly against the CUDA 13.2 headers. Linking was not tried.
findings.evidence: cmake/cuda.cmake:10-11,19,45; ls /usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets shows sbsa-linux only; attach-probe/syntax_check.txt (25/25 rc=0)

findings.topic: CUDA 13 launch handles
findings.detail: In nvcc 13.2, the host code for <<<>>> calls __cudaGetKernel and __cudaLaunchKernel. Those reach cudaLaunchKernel and then cuLaunchKernel carrying a kernel handle, not the host stub address. bpftime looks the kernel up by host address, or by cuFuncGetName. That call returns 400 for this handle, whereas cuKernelGetName would return the name. Result: the original, unpatched kernel runs. This is not specific to Jetson, but CUDA 13.2 is the only toolkit on the board.
findings.evidence: crt/host_runtime.h:113-145; crt/device_functions.h:2937-2975; attach-probe/gdb_launch_trace.txt; nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:165-245,453-471,509-526

findings.topic: Real data flow
findings.detail: With LD_PRELOAD, the agent starts after the executable's constructors have already registered its fatbins. The path that actually runs is therefore the late bootstrap: scan the .nv_fatbin and .nvFatBinSegment sections of loaded files, extract PTX with cuobjdump, patch it, compile with nvPTXCompiler, and load the result with cuModuleLoadDataEx as a separate module. Launches are then redirected by kernel name. The app's own registered fatbin is left untouched.

findings.topic: PTX required
findings.detail: Only PTX can be patched. A fatbin with SASS only yields zero PTX files, and nothing is instrumented. Default nvcc 13.2 output does include PTX (compute_75, .version 9.2). Builds with -arch=native, or with gencode for sm_87 code only, do not. cuBLAS ships PTX for sm_120 only.

findings.topic: Device half verified on sm_87
findings.detail: compose.py repeats bpftime's text edits on CUDA 13.2 PTX: trampoline prepended, headers .version 8.1 / .target sm_87 kept. findings.topic: Host-device channel
findings.detail: Uses cudaHostRegister on the boost shm segment plus cudaHostGetDevicePointer and cuMemHostGetDevicePointer, then computes device addresses as base plus offset. This matters on Orin, where device pointers differ from host pointers (CanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem=0). Sibling tests show that registration and coherence work.

findings.topic: Arch and version assumptions
findings.detail: The passes hard-code sm_61 for LLVM; this is harmless because the PTX headers are replaced. If SM detection fails, the code falls back to sm_61, which CUDA 13 rejects. LLVM 15 does not know sm_87, which affects only the direct-run path. Compile errors raised inside the Boost thread pool are not caught (Boost calls std::terminate).

readers.summary: Area: configuring and building bpftime with -DBPFTIME_ENABLE_CUDA_ATTACH=ON on this Orin (GCC 13, LLVM 15, CUDA 13.2, the RelWithDebInfo + LTO dev configuration). The CUDA toolkit here uses NVIDIA's unified Arm 'SBSA' layout: /usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets holds only sbsa-linux, and include and lib64 are symlinks into it. cmake/cuda.cmake hard-codes targets/aarch64-linux on aarch64. With the stock BPFTIME_CUDA_ROOT=/usr/local/cuda-13.2, configure succeeds (4 s, no warnings), but the build is blocked: compiles fail with 'nvPTXCompiler.h: No such file or directory' (and the same for cuda.h), and links fail with 'cannot find -lcudart / -lcupti / -lnvrtc'. Both failures were reproduced cheaply. Pointing BPFTIME_CUDA_ROOT at a symlink alias root fixes this without editing the repo: targets/aarch64-linux -> sbsa-linux, plus bin, nvvm, version.json, include, lib64 and extras. With that, configure succeeds, CUDA 13.2 is detected, and the 28 CUDA-only translation units (TUs) plus 13 dev-branch TUs that contain CUDA-gated code all pass g++-13 -fsyntax-only against the CUDA 13.2 headers. cuCtxCreate -> v4 is already guarded by #if. A probe link resolves every CUDA library (libcuda through the stubs, SONAME libcuda.so.1 -> L4T driver), and the probe binary runs. The cost is 296 -> 324 TUs (+28), 62 -> 71 link steps, 24 -> 30 links of the static LLVM libraries, and libnvptxcompiler_static.a (about +40 MB) pulled into 20 links. Runtime-relevant CUDA 13 and Orin issues: CUDA 13 dropped sm_61, which bpftime still uses as a fallback; LLVM 15's NVPTX tops out at sm_86 / PTX 7.5; nvcc 13.2 defaults to sm_75. Bottom line: blocked as-is by the CUDA directory layout, and buildable via the alias root (or a 2-line fix in cuda.cmake). No object was compiled with codegen and no bpftime target was linked, so link success, LTO memory use, wall time and runtime behaviour are unverified.

findings.topic: BLOCKER: CUDA 13 SBSA directory layout vs the hard-coded aarch64-linux in cuda.cmake
findings.detail: find_cuda() sets CUDA_TARGET_ARCH=aarch64-linux for aarch64 and derives CUDA_INCLUDE_PATH=<root>/targets/aarch64-linux/include and CUDA_LIBRARY_PATH=<root>/targets/aarch64-linux/lib{,/stubs} plus <root>/extras/CUPTI/lib64. On this board none of these exist: /usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets contains only sbsa-linux, include -> targets/sbsa-linux/include, lib64 -> targets/sbsa-linux/lib, and extras/CUPTI holds only doc/ and samples/. Configure still passes, because find_cuda only errors on an empty root and NVPTXCOMPILER_LIB is found through the second search path <root>/lib64, so the failure first appears at compile/link time. -lcuda alone resolves, through /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> /opt/nvidia/l4t-gpu-libs/nvgpu/libcuda.so. Passing /usr/local/cuda instead of /usr/local/cuda-13.2 fails the same way. Upstream has no mention of sbsa anywhere.
findings.evidence: cmake/cuda.cmake:10-11,19,41-45,50,59-60; `ls -la /usr/local/cuda-13.2/` -> 'include -> targets/sbsa-linux/include', 'lib64 -> targets/sbsa-linux/lib', targets/ has only sbsa-linux; stock-root configure (scratch build-stockroot) compile_commands shows '-I/usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets/aarch64-linux/include' '-I/usr/local/cuda-13.2/cuda-13.2/extras/CUPTI/include'; preprocessing ptx_compiler.cpp with that command -> 'ptx_compiler.cpp:1:10: fatal error: nvPTXCompiler.h: No such file or directory'; `g++-13 m.cpp -L<those dirs> -lcuda -lcudart -lcupti -lnvrtc` -> '/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcudart', '-lcupti', '-lnvrtc'; `git grep -i sbsa official/master` -> no output

findings.topic: Workaround: symlink alias CUDA root (no repo edit); configure verified, real link unverified
findings.detail: Alias root layout: <A>/targets/aarch64-linux -> /usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets/sbsa-linux, plus <A>/{bin,nvvm,version.json,include,lib64,extras} -> /usr/local/cuda-13.2/*. Do not alias extras/CUPTI/lib64: CUPTI is unused (see the dependencies finding), and without it CMake links -lcupti dynamically, which --as-needed then drops. Configure prints 'Detected CUDA version: 13.2' (parsed from version.json, 'cuda' version 13.2.2), 'Using cupti (dynamic library)', and 'runtime CUDA libs= cuda;cudart;<A>/targets/aarch64-linux/lib/libnvptxcompiler_static.a;cupti;nvrtc'. The build RUNPATH and the cached NVPTXCOMPILER_LIB:FILEPATH both embed <A>, so put the alias at a persistent path, not /tmp. If <A> disappears later, the binaries still resolve their libraries through ld.so.conf, which lists /usr/local/cuda/targets/sbsa-linux/lib and /opt/nvidia/l4t-gpu-libs/nvgpu. A scratch alias plus a configured scratch build dir already exist (paths in open_questions).

findings.topic: Proper fix (small upstream PR candidate)
findings.detail: In find_cuda, after picking aarch64-linux: if <root>/targets/aarch64-linux does not exist and <root>/targets/sbsa-linux does, use sbsa-linux. Also fall back to targets/<arch>/include and targets/<arch>/lib for CUPTI, which lives there in CUDA 13 instead of extras/CUPTI. This is about 2-6 lines in cmake/cuda.cmake. findings.topic: CUDA 13 API compatibility at compile level (verified with -fsyntax-only)
findings.detail: All 28 CUDA-only TUs pass syntax-only compilation with the exact compile_commands flags from the alias-root configure (g++-13, CUDA 13.2 headers, LLVM 15). That covers nv_attach_impl x7, ptxpass_core x2, the 3 pass main.cpp files, ptx_compiler, the 3 nv tests, 9 runtime GPU sources, test_cuda_compile.cpp and 2 GPU benchmarks. So do 13 dev-branch TUs that contain CUDA-gated code: bpftime_prog.cpp, bpftime_shm.cpp, bpftime_shm_internal.cpp, bpf_attach_ctx.cpp, bpftime_prog_cache.cpp, prog_handler.cpp, the three syscall-server sources, agent.cpp, bpftimetool main.cpp, test_aot_cache.cpp and test_prog_jit_load.cpp. The only diagnostic was one -Wunused-but-set-variable. CUDA 13's cuCtxCreate -> cuCtxCreate_v4 (4 args) is handled by #if CUDA_VERSION >= 13000 at every call site in the main tree. The explicit _v2 names used (cuCtxPushCurrent_v2, cuMemcpyDtoHAsync_v2, cuMemcpyHtoDAsync_v2, cuGraph*KernelNode*_v2) and CUDA_KERNEL_NODE_PARAMS_v1/_v2 all exist in the 13.2 cuda.h. Front-end time for the 28 CUDA TUs was about 161 s on one core. The one remaining 3-argument cuCtxCreate is in the PTX example, which is built only with LLVMBPF_ENABLE_PTX=ON (default OFF).

findings.topic: CUDA 13 dropped sm_61 (and everything below sm_75), but bpftime still uses sm_61
findings.detail: ptxas 13.2 rejects --gpu-name=sm_61, and nvcc 13.2 supports only compute_75 and newer. get_gpu_sm_arch() returns 'sm_61' whenever cuInit, cuDeviceGet or cuDeviceGetAttribute fails, and that string goes straight to nvPTXCompiler as --gpu-name, which would then fail under CUDA 13. In normal operation detection returns sm_87. The PTX passes compile eBPF -> PTX with a hard-coded 'sm_61'. That works, because the pass output has its .version/.target headers stripped and the final PTX's .target is rewritten to the detected arch: verified that PTX from LLVM 15 for sm_61, compiled with --gpu-name=sm_87, assembles. The trampoline Makefile also defaults to sm_61, but it is not part of the CMake build.
findings.evidence: `ptxas --gpu-name=sm_61 -c t_sm_61.ptx` -> 'ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_61' is not defined for option 'gpu-name''; `ptxas --gpu-name=sm_87 -c t_sm_61.ptx` -> ok; `nvcc --list-gpu-arch` -> 'compute_75 compute_80 compute_86 compute_87 ...'; attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_utils.cpp:118-149; nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:107,127,149; pass/ptxpass_kprobe_entry/main.cpp:55, ptxpass_kretprobe/main.cpp:43, ptxpass_kprobe_memcapture/main.cpp:141; trampoline/Makefile:3
findings.why_risky: Any failure of CUDA detection inside a traced process turns into a confusing PTX compile error instead of a clear error.

findings.topic: LLVM 15 NVPTX has no sm_87 (stops at sm_86 / PTX 7.5)
findings.detail: llc-15 -mcpu=help lists processors up to sm_86 and PTX up to ptx75. With -mcpu=sm_87, LLVM 15 prints "'sm_87' is not a recognized processor" six times on stderr and emits '.version 3.2 .target sm_87', which ptxas 13.2 rejects. The direct-run path (run program on GPU) passes the detected sm_arch to LLVM. Its LLVM header is stripped and replaced by the trampoline's '.version 8.1' (target rewritten to sm_87), so it probably assembles, but LLVM's warnings land on the traced process's stderr, which the CLAUDE.md host-process contract forbids. Separately, rewrite_ptx_target raises .version only for sm_100 and above; an LLVM-15 sm_61 header (.version 5.0) that kept .target sm_87 would fail, though current code paths strip it. Two escape hatches, both verified: (a) BPFTIME_SM_ARCH=sm_86 (LLVM 15 emits .version 7.1 .target sm_86, and a cubin containing only sm_86 SASS ran correctly on this Orin); (b) configure with LLVM 16, whose llc knows sm_87 and emits .version 7.4. Option (b) changes the toolchain the dev results were measured with.
findings.evidence: `llc-15 -march=nvptx64 -mcpu=help` (list ends sm_86, ptx75); `llc-15 -mcpu=sm_87 t.ll` -> 6x "'sm_87' is not a recognized processor for this target (ignoring processor)", '.version 3.2' '.target sm_87'; `ptxas --gpu-name=sm_87 t_sm_87.ptx` -> 'PTX .version 3.2 does not support .target sm_87'; t_v50_sm87.ptx -> 'PTX .version 5.0 does not support .target sm_87'; '.version 8.1 .target sm_87' -> assembles; attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:1128-1143; pass/ptxpass_core/src/core.cpp:165-190,228-229; nv_attach_utils.cpp:30-43,62-66; sm86test: `nvcc -gencode arch=compute_86,code=sm_86` -> cuobjdump shows only sm_86 ELF, run -> 'launch=no error sync=no error h[63]=64'; `llc-16 -mcpu=sm_87` -> '.version 7.4 .target sm_87'; /usr/lib/llvm-16/lib/cmake/llvm exists
findings.why_risky: The direct-run path works only because of header replacement, and LLVM writes to the host's stderr.

findings.topic: A fresh build dir is required; BPFTIME_CUDA_ROOT is a BOOL option() holding a path
findings.detail: StandardSettings declares BPFTIME_CUDA_ROOT with option(), so the cache stores it as BOOL. A path given with -D works, because if(NOT path) is false and ${} expands the path. Existing dev caches hold 'BPFTIME_CUDA_ROOT:BOOL=OFF'. add_compile_definitions(BPFTIME_ENABLE_CUDA_ATTACH=1) is global and reaches 213 of 324 compile commands, and NVPTXCOMPILER_LIB is cached once with find_library. Never reuse build-jetson-daily or the other build-* dirs. Other requirements: BPFTIME_LLVM_JIT must be ON (nv_attach_impl depends on llvmbpf_vm), and Frida is forced ON on aarch64.

findings.topic: Do not `cmake --install` the CUDA build
findings.detail: The install destination is hard-coded to $HOME/.bpftime for bpftime-agent, bpftime_text_segment_transformer and bpftime-syscall-server, and tools/daemon install there too. findings.topic: A CUDA build changes non-GPU processes (keep it out of uprobe/syscall measurements and the daily gate)
findings.detail: Every binary that links runtime (19 targets, plus ptx_compiler) pulls libnvptxcompiler_static.a: a toy program calling only nvPTXCompilerGetVersion was 43.7 MB. Upstream never builds bpftime_runtime_tests with CUDA ON. The size of these effects is unmeasured.

findings.topic: Include-order ODR gap with the dev branch's patched llvmbpf.hpp
findings.detail: nv_attach_impl lists vm/llvm-jit/include in its own include dirs, ahead of llvmbpf_vm's interface dir that holds the patched llvmbpf.hpp (array-inline-include). So nv_attach_impl_patcher.cpp compiles against the unpatched header, while ptxpass_core/src/core.cpp, which constructs bpftime::llvmbpf_vm, and compat_llvm.cpp get the patched one. The patcher only uses string helpers, so in practice this is harmless today. It still breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that every VM consumer uses the generated descriptor header, and it could show up as -Wodr under LTO. runtime/CMakeLists.txt:195 adds the same unpatched dir PUBLIC, but no runtime TU includes llvmbpf.hpp (grep).

findings.topic: Link-line structure (generated, not executed): whole-archive dedup, archive cycle, PIC
findings.detail: CMake deduplicates link options, so in the agent and syscall-server links libbpftime_nv_attach_impl.a, libbpftime_llvm_vm.a, libbpftime_vm.a and libllvmbpf_vm.a end up outside --whole-archive. This is harmless: nv_attach_impl has no constructor/registrar, and the agent compiles bpftime_llvm_vm_obj objects in directly. The behaviour comes from upstream. readers.summary: bpftime's CUDA support works like this. It Frida-hooks libcudart's __cudaRegisterFatBinary, __cudaRegisterFunction and cudaLaunchKernel, plus libcuda's cuLaunchKernel and cuGraph*. It pulls the app's PTX out with cuobjdump, injects eBPF compiled by LLVM-15 NVPTX plus a trampoline, recompiles with nvPTXCompiler for the detected SM, and sends launches to the patched module. GPU helpers reach the host through a cudaHostRegister'ed slice of the bpftime shm, which a watcher thread in the agent polls. On this Orin (cc 8.7, 8 SMs, 7.5 GB, CUDA 13.2 with the sbsa layout) I tested the primitives that path needs with scratch programs, and they all work: cudaHostRegister of a MAP_SHARED shm at 20/128/256 MB, device pointers, a GPU<->CPU flag handshake, GPU atomics on that memory, %globaltimer, PTX extraction, and the merged trampoline+app PTX compiling for sm_87. Four things stand in the way. (1) The CUDA build needs a shadow CUDA root, because cmake/cuda.cmake hard-codes targets/aarch64-linux but this toolkit only has targets/sbsa-linux. (2) cuIpcGetMemHandle returns CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED (801), so every example using GPU_ARRAY_MAP (1503) or PERGPUTD_ARRAY_MAP (1502) fails at map creation: threadhist, launchlate, mem_trace, gpu_shared_map, atomizer, directly_run_on_gpu, cutlass, faiss/llama/pytorch, benchmark/gpu/micro and benchmark/gpu/host. (3) CUDA 13.2 host stubs launch through a cudaKernel_t handle (__cudaGetKernel/__cudaLaunchKernel). That handle misses bpftime's main lookup, which is keyed by the host stub. Probes then fire only if the by-name cuLaunchKernel fallback works, and it only runs after a 'late bootstrap' step finishes at agent start. This is unverified. Building the victim with -D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH -Xcompiler -D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH forces the old path; I verified it changes the import to cudaLaunchKernel, so it gives a clean A/B. (4) The sm_61 fallback is rejected by CUDA 13.2, so pin BPFTIME_SM_ARCH=sm_87. The first examples to try all keep their data in host memory: kernelretsnoop (device-only helpers + GPU ringbuf), cuda-counter (host-call helpers + HASH maps), host_map_test (host-backed maps made for Tegra, exact per-thread counts), kernel_trace and cudagraph. benchmark/gpu/workload/vec_add has the same _Z9vectorAddPKfS0_Pf kernel but finishes on its own, so runs stay bounded and have exact expected counts. Nothing was built or changed in the repo; all experiments are under /tmp/claude-2002/-home-jetson-src/6ac0883f-4479-466c-bec5-5fa31cffe4de/scratchpad/gpu-env.

findings.topic: PTX pipeline on CUDA 13.2 / sm_87
findings.detail: Examples compile with `nvcc -cudart shared X.cu -o X -g` and no -arch. nvcc 13.2 then emits sm_75 SASS plus compute_75 PTX (.version 9.2, .target sm_75). Driver JIT runs the uninstrumented binary fine here: plain vec_add printed correct results. bpftime's pipeline: (1) cuobjdump --extract-ptx all, run through posix_spawn of /bin/sh with LD_PRELOAD cleared; cuobjdump is found via BPFTIME_CUOBJDUMP, BPFTIME_CUDA_ROOT/CUDA_HOME/... or /usr/local/cuda*/bin. (2) Per hook, the ptxpass_kprobe_entry/kretprobe/memcapture .so (loaded with dlmopen) compiles the eBPF to PTX with LLVM NVPTX at 'sm_61' and injects calls. (3) trampoline_ptx.h (.version 8.1 / .target sm_61) is prepended, and filter_out_version_headers_ptx keeps only the first .version/.target. (4) rewrite_ptx_target sets .target to the detected SM (it changes .version only for sm>=100). (5) nvPTXCompiler with --gpu-name=sm_87 -O3, then cuModuleLoadDataEx, then constData/map_info are copied in. I emulated steps 3-4 for cuda-counter's vec_add (trampoline + extracted PTX -> .version 8.1/.target sm_87) and it compiles with ptxas -arch=sm_87 (rc=0; vectorAdd REG:12). Not covered: the LLVM-15-generated eBPF function text. Caveat: the app body is compiled under the trampoline's .version 8.1 although the app was 9.2. That is fine for vec_add, but a victim using newer PTX syntax could fail.

findings.topic: CUDA 13.2 kernel launches pass a cudaKernel_t handle, not the host stub; this is the main risk that probes do not fire
findings.detail: With nvcc 13.2 defaults (no __NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH), the host stub calls __cudaGetKernel(&handle, stub) once and then __cudaLaunchKernel(handle, ...). In libcudart.so.13, __cudaLaunchKernel is a five-instruction thunk that branches straight into cudaLaunchKernel, so bpftime's Frida replacement does run, but with func = handle. Measured here: handle 0xaaaaf1da6a00 vs stub 0xaaaad5c5141c. bpftime's main path looks up symbol_address_to_fatbin, which is keyed by the host stub from __cudaRegisterFunction, so it misses. The next path is gated on late bootstrap; it tries dladdr on the handle and will almost certainly miss too. What remains: cudart calls the exported libcuda cuLaunchKernel (confirmed with gdb). bpftime replaces that function too; its replacement maps the CUfunction to a name with cuFuncGetName and swaps in the patched function, but only if is_late_bootstrap_done(). Late bootstrap runs at attach time inside the agent: it scans .nv_fatbin (present in these victims), runs cuobjdump, and pre-loads patched kernels. So on CUDA 13 the probe depends on that bootstrap succeeding. Otherwise patch logs look healthy while the original kernel runs: no events, no error. Verified workaround/control: compile victims with `-D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH -Xcompiler -D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH`. The binary then imports plain cudaLaunchKernel and passes the host stub. -D alone does not compile, because nvcc does not forward it to the final host compile of .cudafe1.cpp. Upstream's CUDA-13 commit only claims that the injected PTX compiles. Debug-level discriminators: "Launching kernel.." means the main path hit; "Late attach launch: unable to resolve host function" means the handle missed. The cuLaunchKernel path logs nothing on success, so judge it by probe data.

findings.topic: Hook targets on aarch64 / CUDA 13.2

No x86-only constructs in attach/nv_attach_impl: no user_regs_struct; process_vm_readv and PTRACE_PEEKDATA are generic. Frida inline hooks on small libcudart functions (__cudaRegisterFatBinary is 40 bytes) are untested on this build.

findings.detail: These agent logs (stderr) are necessary but do not prove the probe ran: "Recorded pass <...>/ptxpass_kretprobe... for func _Z9vectorAddPKfS0_Pf", "Got 1 PTX files", "Patching PTX: vec_add.1.sm_75.ptx", "Compiling PTXs with sm_arch sm_87", "Compile of patched.vec_add.1.sm_75.ptx done", "Loaded module: patched.vec_add.1.sm_75.ptx", "Registered shared memory with CUDA: addr=... size=...", "CommSharedMem host ... mapped to device ...", "nv_attach_impl: late attach bootstrap ingested 1 fatbin(s)" (this one arms the CUDA-13 fallback), and "Mapped GPU memory for gpu ringbuf map" / "Mapped shared memory for GPU access". (shm name mismatch or a non-CUDA server), "CUDA shared communication memory not available; CUDA attach will be disabled", "No pass definition matched", "Unable to compile:", "Unable to launch kernel:" (after which the original kernel runs silently), "cudaHostRegister() failed". findings.topic: Ranked first tries, with expected proof output
findings.detail: All five avoid CUDA IPC. 1) kernelretsnoop: device-only helpers (505 thread idx, 502 globaltimer) plus bpf_perf_event_output into GPU_RINGBUF, with no host-call helper. With the finite workload `vec_add 5 3 5 1` (4 launches x 5 threads), expect exactly 20 lines "Thread (x, 0, 0) timestamp: ~1.18e15", 4 for each x in 0..4. 2) cuda-counter: adds the host-call helper path (HASH maps, bpf_printk). With workload `vec_add 10 5 10 1` (6 launches x 10 threads), the server prints "<TAB>pid=<victim pid> <TAB>calls: N" with N in 51..60. The first launch's 10 threads race on BPF_NOEXIST and add 1-10; each later launch adds +10 through atomics, which I verified on registered memory. With BPFTIME_TRACE_PRINTK_OUTPUT=stdout the victim log has 60 "Entered _Z9vectorAddPKfS0_Pf x=0, ts=~1.18e15" and 60 "Exited (with tsp) ..." lines. Negative control (victim without the agent): no "calls:" line. 3) host_map_test: host-backed maps 1512/1513, designed for Tegra, with on-device map access. With workload `vec_add 10 5 10 1`, the final block should read: shared_counter "key=0..9 value: 6"; perthread "key=0  (call_count): total=60 (from 10 threads)" and "key=2  (thread_id): total=45 (from 9 threads)" (thread 0 writes 0, so it is not counted); thread_timestamp "key=0: 10 threads have timestamps". Leave BPFTIME_MAP_GPU_THREAD_COUNT unset: host maps size from attr.gpu_thread_count=1024, while the loader reads the env var. 4) kernel_trace: kprobe at entry plus ringbuf; it samples only block0/thread0 of its own 4-argument kernel (32x128 threads, infinite loop). Use CI env BPFTIME_MAP_GPU_THREAD_COUNT=4096, BPFTIME_SHM_MEMORY_MB=256. Expect one "[kernel_trace] ts=~1.18e15 block=(0,0,0) thread=(0,0,0)" per launch and "[kernel_trace] total events: N" growing; the victim prints "vectorAdd => C[0]=0.0 C[1]=4.0". 5) cudagraph: graph-node hooks, leader thread only. With BPFTIME_CUDAGRAPH_ITERS=5, expect a final "calls: 6" (1 stream launch + 5 graph launches). 5 means the stream launch was missed (the CUDA-13 handle path); 1 means graph launches were not instrumented. Then run the legacy-launch A/B on anything that shows zero events. Optional 6th: threadscheduling (SM ids must be 0-7, "Total threads: 256"). Run shape for all of them, matching CI and the 'timeout outside LD_PRELOAD' rule: a separate BPFTIME_GLOBAL_SHM_NAME per example; start the server first and give it 5 s; wrap each process as `timeout -k 5 -s INT N env LD_PRELOAD=... prog`; use SIGINT so loaders flush stdout (kernelretsnoop has no setvbuf); check for leftovers with pgrep -x afterwards; avoid the ~03:30 JST daily-timer window.

findings.topic: Unit tests that can run here
findings.detail: bpftime_nv_attach_tests (attach/nv_attach_impl/test: nv_attach_impl_tests.cpp, test_ptxpass.cpp, test_register_guard.cpp; test_kernel_finder.cpp is commented out) is host-only: string filters, the JSON pass protocol, AttachPointMatcher, eBPF->PTX through LLVM NVPTX (llc-15 lists nvptx/nvptx64), and the register guard. It needs no GPU, only the CUDA_ATTACH=ON build, because it links bpftime_nv_attach_impl plus libcuda, cudart, nvrtc and cupti, all present via ldconfig. CI runs it as ./build/attach/nv_attach_impl/test/bpftime_nv_attach_tests. bpftime_runtime_tests in a CUDA build adds runtime/unit-test/cuda/test_cuda_compile.cpp. "Test cuda compile" only loads a *__cuda-named program; the CUDA compile code in bpftime_prog.cpp is commented out, so it does not touch the GPU. "CUDA watcher stops before shared-memory teardown" builds bpf_attach_ctx in a SHM_REMOVE_AND_CREATE process, where the segment is never cudaHostRegister'ed (registration happens only in SHM_OPEN_ONLY). CUDAContext then calls cudaHostGetDevicePointer, which returned 'invalid argument' on an unregistered shm here, so expect a throw ("Unable to get device pointer for CommSharedMem"). The same applies to any creator-mode process that constructs bpf_attach_ctx in a CUDA build, so keep the CUDA build separate from the daily regression build. Run runtime tests with a private BPFTIME_GLOBAL_SHM_NAME, because SHM_REMOVE_AND_CREATE deletes the named segment. The vm test "Test NVPTX target is registered" (vm_test.cpp:500-512) is GPU-free and already runs in the normal build.

readers.summary: Area: the CUDA environment on this Jetson Orin, measured with small programs (sources, binaries and raw logs are in /tmp/claude-2002/-home-jetson-src/6ac0883f-4479-466c-bec5-5fa31cffe4de/scratchpad/gpu-env, abbreviated GE below). Repo paths are relative to /home/jetson/src/bpftime-daily-state/worktrees/177a1dc465ff/candidate, read-only. The device is an "Orin" iGPU: cc 8.7, 8 SMs, 7.36 GiB shared memory, driver and runtime 13020. Bottom line: the memory model bpftime's GPU path depends on works on this board. Two processes can map the same /dev/shm MAP_SHARED file. cudaHostRegister works on it (4 MiB and the default 128 MiB, every flag variant, and also under RLIMIT_MEMLOCK=0). Interior device pointers keep their offsets. Each process sees the other's writes in both directions. Running the shipped helper-call handshake while the kernel runs gives 0 stale reads in 2000 rounds (about 4.9 us per round trip), and 1024 serialized calls from 1024 threads all succeed. GPU atomics running alongside CPU atomics lose nothing. The toolchain also accepts what bpftime ships: the driver JIT and nvPTXCompiler 13.2 compile, load and run PTX with .target sm_60..sm_87. The shipped trampoline PTX (8.1/sm_61) compiles as-is and after the sm_87 rewrite. Emulating bpftime's header merging, the result still compiles and runs. The real risks are elsewhere. (1) canUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem=0: a raw host pointer used in a kernel is an illegal address. (2) nvcc's default build links cudart statically, so cudaMalloc and __cudaRegisterFatBinary are not exported symbols. (3) -arch=native and code=sm_87-only builds carry no PTX. (4) The toolkit layout is targets/sbsa-linux only, which bpftime's cmake does not expect. (5) LLVM 15 cannot target sm_87 and tops out at ptx75. This is harmless today because bpftime strips LLVM's PTX header. The ceilings are PTX ISA 9.2 and .target sm_87. One case is unverified: cuMemHostRegister on an mmapped kernel BPF array map needs CAP_BPF, and I did not use sudo. Caveat: sibling agents shared the GE directory and may have used the GPU between 01:36 and 01:52, so latencies are indicative only. Correctness results are not affected.

findings.detail: name=Orin, cc 8.7, multiProcessorCount=8, maxThreadsPerBlock=1024, maxThreadsPerMultiProcessor=1536, maxBlocksPerMultiprocessor=16, l2CacheSize=4194304 (persisting max 2883584), totalGlobalMem=7899594752 (shared with CPU; cudaMemGetInfo free=4104245248), warp 32, clock 1020000 kHz. integrated=1, unifiedAddressing=1, canMapHostMemory=1, pageableMemoryAccess=0, pageableMemoryAccessUsesHostPageTables=0, concurrentManagedAccess=0, hostRegisterSupported=1, canUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem=0, managedMemory=1, computePreemptionSupported=1, cooperativeLaunch=1. Extras: hostNativeAtomicSupported=1, directManagedMemAccessFromHost=0, KernelExecTimeout=0 (no watchdog), HostRegisterReadOnlySupported=1, MemoryPoolsSupported=1, VIRTUAL_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT=1, asyncEngineCount=2. The driver API returns the same values as the runtime API.
findings.evidence: GE/attrs.out.txt (timeout 60 ./attrs, built with nvcc -arch=sm_87 attrs.cu -lcuda): 'cudaDriverGetVersion=13020 cudaRuntimeGetVersion=13020', 'cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem = 0', 'cudaDevAttrPageableMemoryAccess = 0', 'cudaDevAttrConcurrentManagedAccess = 0'
findings.why_risky: Informational. The attributes that matter are covered in separate findings: canUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem=0, pageableMemoryAccess=0 (plain malloc memory must be registered before the GPU can touch it) and concurrentManagedAccess=0.

findings.topic: (2b) /dev/shm MAP_SHARED + cudaHostRegister, bpftime-shaped
findings.detail: A file in /dev/shm, mmapped MAP_SHARED, registers fine at both sizes and with all flag variants. Register time: 4 MiB 0.98 ms; 128 MiB (bpftime default, bpftime_config.hpp:81) 16.05 ms prefaulted and 16.49 ms not prefaulted. Unregister: 0.20 ms and 3.8 ms. Flags tried: cudaHostRegisterMapped; cudaHostRegisterDefault (cudaHostGetFlags still reports 0x2, i.e. mapped implicitly); Portable|Mapped (0x3); driver cuMemHostRegister(PORTABLE|DEVICEMAP). Device base is 0x1021c4000, not the host VA. cudaHostGetDevicePointer on base+4112 returns devbase+4112, and on the last u32 the offset is also preserved. Visibility, after the kernel finishes: (a) a kernel writes one u32 in each of the 32768 pages; the same-process CPU sees 0 mismatches, and a second process (shmtool, no CUDA) mapping the same file also sees 0 mismatches. (b) The second process writes every page; the GPU reads them with 0 mismatches.
findings.evidence: GE/hostreg.shm.txt ('timeout 60 ./hostreg shm 128 mapped'): 'register took 16.052 ms', 'interior +4112: dev=0x1021c5010 expected=0x1021c5010 OK', '[shmtool] check n=32768 stride=1024 add=0x1000 mismatches=0', 'GPU reads second-process writes: ... mismatches=0 of 32768'. Same results for 'default', 'portmap' and 'drv'. Mirrors runtime/src/bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1405-1424 and runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu_kernel_shared/array_map_kernel_gpu.cpp:257-272 (offset arithmetic) and :288-302.
findings.why_risky: Positive result. It confirms the core assumption of the boost-interprocess + cudaHostRegister design.

findings.topic: (2a) cudaHostRegister on malloc, stack and static memory
findings.detail: Every case registers, gets a device pointer, and a kernel read/write through that pointer is seen by the CPU with 0 mismatches. Cases: 64 KiB posix_memalign (Mapped / Default / Portable|Mapped / cuMemHostRegister); malloc(40), unaligned at 0x...170; malloc(1 MiB), an mmap chunk at +0x570; a 4-byte stack int (the default_trampoline.cu:582-584 pattern); a 4-byte static .data int. The device pointer is never equal to the host pointer, and the page offset is kept (host ...f00 maps to device ...f00).
findings.evidence: GE/hostreg.malloc.txt ('timeout 60 ./hostreg malloc'): '[G stack int (4 bytes), Mapped] ... cudaHostRegister -> 0 no error ... CPU sees GPU writes: mismatches=0 of 1'; 'final cudaGetLastError=no error'
findings.why_risky: Positive result.

findings.topic: canUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem=0: raw host pointer faults
findings.detail: A kernel that dereferences the host VA of registered /dev/shm memory (instead of the cudaHostGetDevicePointer result) fails with 'an illegal memory access was encountered'. The error is sticky and kills the context. nvgpu logs it as an SM machine check. The bpftime paths I grepped all translate the pointer: bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:412, nv_gpu_array_host_map.cpp:33, nv_gpu_shared_array_host_map.cpp:127, nv_gpu_ringbuf_map.cpp:37, array_map_kernel_gpu.cpp:257-272/302.
findings.evidence: GE/hostreg.hostptr.txt: 'host=0xffff95b30000 dev=0x1021c4000; launching kernel on the HOST pointer ... sync=an illegal memory access was encountered'. journalctl -k: 'nvgpu_gr_intr_handle_sm_exception:347 [ERR] sm machine check err. gpc_id(0), tpc_id(3)' and 'error notifier set to 13 for ch 2043 owned by hostreg'
findings.why_risky: Any bpftime path that puts a host VA into GPU-visible state without translating it will fault here. Example: a map pointer written into map_info[].extra_buffer or constData. On x86 dGPU setups the registered host pointer is often usable as-is (general CUDA behaviour, not measured here), so such bugs can pass x86 testing.

findings.topic: Live GPU<->CPU handshake (helper-call protocol) while the kernel runs
findings.detail: Single round trip: the kernel stores flag1, then spins on flag2 while a host thread answers. All 3 variants ('bpf' = the exact default_trampoline.cu:149-162 asm, membar.sys + weak ld.global; 'vol'; 'none' = no fences) work on all 3 memory kinds (registered shm, cudaHostAlloc, registered malloc), and also when the host side is a different process. Time inside the kernel was 3.2-5.5 us with 1-2 spins. Multi-round with payload: 2000 rounds, bpf-exact, the host writes resp=3*id+1 and the GPU does a plain load. done=2000, stale_resp=0, avg 4.90 us, max 23.10 us ('vol': avg 4.78, max 11.36). Many threads serialized like make_helper_call (per-lane loop + atomicCAS lock in device memory): 1x32, 4x64 and 8x128 threads gave ok=32/256/1024, bad=0, timed_out=0; 1024 calls took 6.1 ms wall. Mechanism: on sm_87, membar.sys compiles to MEMBAR.SC.SYS; ERRBAR; CCTL.IVALL (L1 invalidate). The shipped trampoline's make_helper_call, compiled by ptxas 13.2 for sm_87, has the same sequence around each poll.
findings.evidence: GE/hostreg.hs.txt, GE/hostreg.hsloop-atomdev.txt ('[hsloop variant=bpf rounds=2000] ... done=2000 stale_resp=0 ... avg_roundtrip=4.90 us max_roundtrip=23.10 us'), GE/hostreg.hsmulti.txt ('[hsmulti 8x128] ... ok=1024 bad=0 timed_out=0 host_served=1024 wall=6.100 ms'). 'cuobjdump -sass GE/cubin/trampoline_reloc_sm87.cubin' (from 'ptxas -c --gpu-name=sm_87 repo_ptx/trampoline_rewritten_sm87.ptx'): make_helper_call contains 'MEMBAR.SC.SYS ; ERRBAR; CCTL.IVALL ; STG.E [R22.64], R5' and 'MEMBAR.SC.SYS ... LDG.E R0, [R22.64+0x4]'
findings.why_risky: Positive result: the iGPU/CPU coherence that bpftime's helper calls need holds here. Untested: very long-running spins under contention from other GPU clients. Xorg and gnome-shell hold GPU channels; tsg_timeslice_max_us=50000.

findings.topic: GPU atomics on registered host memory
findings.detail: GPU-only test: atomicAdd on u32 and u64 in registered shm, 8x256 threads x 100 iterations, both counters = 204800 as expected. Concurrent test: GPU atomicAdd_system (2,048,000 adds) against CPU __atomic_fetch_add (2,000,000) gave total 4048000, lost 0, and the time windows overlapped (GPU 0-67 ms, CPU 0.1-82.5 ms). Device-scope atomicAdd (what LLVM emits for eBPF atomics) against CPU atomics: u32 and u64 both lost 0. A CAS spinlock living in host memory gave counter 1600 of 1600.
findings.evidence: GE/hostreg.atom-dual.txt: '[atom CPU+GPU] ... total=4048000 expected=4048000 lost=0'. GE/hostreg.hsloop-atomdev.txt: '[atomdev CPU+GPU device-scope atomicAdd] ... lost32=0 lost64=0'
findings.why_risky: Positive result (hostNativeAtomicSupported=1).

findings.topic: Two processes registering the same /dev/shm file at once
findings.detail: Process A registers a 4 MiB mapping and keeps it. Process B, spawned while A still holds its registration, maps the same file, registers it (it gets the same GPU VA, 0x1021c4000, in its own address space), and its kernel adds 0x20000 to every page. A's CPU and A's GPU (through A's device pointer) both see B's GPU writes, 0 mismatches of 1024.
findings.evidence: GE/hostreg.atom-dual.txt: '[A] A-CPU sees B-GPU writes: mismatches=0 of 1024', '[A] A-GPU sees B-GPU writes: sync=no error mismatches=0 of 1024'
findings.why_risky: Positive result: server and agent processes can both pin the segment.

findings.topic: RLIMIT_MEMLOCK does not limit cudaHostRegister here
findings.detail: Registering 128 MiB of /dev/shm (and the GPU/CPU/second-process checks) succeeds with memlock limits of 8 MiB, 64 KiB and 0. Register times were 12.4, 16.3 and 19.4 ms. The interactive shell's own limit is 964304 KB.
findings.evidence: GE/memlock.txt ('timeout 60 prlimit --memlock=0:0 sh -c ... ./hostreg shm 128 mapped'): 'ulimit -l inside: 0', 'register took 19.383 ms', 'second-process check exit=0'; GE/env0.txt
findings.why_risky: Positive result: injecting into a service with a small memlock limit should still work.

findings.topic: Registration edge cases
findings.detail: cudaSetDeviceFlags(cudaDeviceMapHost) after the context already exists returned 0, and flags became 0x8. Registering from a std::thread and then using the memory from the main thread works. Registering a sub-range of an already registered range, or the same range again, returns 712 'part or all of the requested memory range is already mapped'; it is not sticky (cleared by cudaGetLastError). On a PROT_READ MAP_SHARED mapping, cudaHostRegister(Mapped) returns 1 'invalid argument', but Mapped|ReadOnly works and the kernel reads correctly.
findings.evidence: GE/misc.out.txt ('timeout 60 ./misc')
findings.why_risky: This only matters if bpftime ever registers sub-ranges of the segment it has already registered (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1424 registers the whole segment), or registers a read-only mapping.

findings.topic: (3) PTX JIT and nvPTXCompiler: older targets accepted, ceilings
findings.detail: Tested a minimal kernel PTX across version/target pairs on three paths: driver JIT (cuModuleLoadData and cuModuleLoadDataEx with logs), static nvPTXCompiler 13.2 with --gpu-name=sm_87 --verbose (the nv_attach_impl.cpp:1175-1177 options) followed by loading the ELF, and the ptxas CLI. Compiled, loaded and RAN (value 42): 5.0/sm_60, 7.0/sm_60, 8.1/sm_60, 5.0/sm_61, 8.1/sm_61, 6.0/sm_70, 8.1/sm_70, 6.1/sm_72, 8.1/sm_72, 6.3/sm_75, 8.1/sm_75, 9.2/sm_75, 7.0/sm_80, 9.2/sm_80, 7.1/sm_86, 9.2/sm_86, and 7.4, 7.5, 7.8, 8.1, 8.5, 9.0, 9.1, 9.2 with sm_87. Rejected: .version 5.0/7.0/7.3 with sm_87 (218, 'PTX .version 7.3 does not support .target sm_87'); 9.2 with sm_88/sm_89/sm_90 (218, 'SM version specified by .target is higher than default SM version assumed'); .version 9.3, 9.4, 9.5 and 10.0 (222 CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PTX_VERSION, 'current version is 9.2'). Repo PTX: trampoline_ptx.h (8.1/sm_61, 44072 B ELF) and demo_ptx_prog.hpp (8.1/sm_60) compile and load both as-is and with .target rewritten to sm_87. The attach_impl test fragment (5.0/sm_60) fails only on an unresolved extern '_bpf_helper_ext_0001' (expected for a fragment); rewritten to sm_87 it fails on the .version check.
findings.evidence: GE/ptxprobe.out.txt ('timeout 120 ./ptxprobe ptx_ladder/*.ptx repo_ptx/*.ptx'), e.g. 'v8.1_sm_61.ptx P2[nvPTXCompiler]: compile OK elf=3368B; load(ELF)=no error; ... value=42 RAN-OK' and 'P3[driver JIT]: load(PTX)=0 ... RAN-OK'. GE/ptxas.ladder.txt. Sources: attach/nv_attach_impl/trampoline_ptx.h:6-7, runtime/src/attach/demo_ptx_prog.hpp:9-10, attach/nv_attach_impl/test/nv_attach_impl_tests.cpp:11-12
findings.why_risky: Positive result: driver JIT forward compatibility from sm_60 PTX works. The hard limits are .version<=9.2, .target<=sm_87, and .version>=7.4 whenever .target is sm_87.

findings.topic: (4) PTX ISA version: ptxas ceiling and nvcc default
findings.detail: ptxas 13.2 (V13.2.86) and nvPTXCompilerGetVersion=13.2 both accept at most .version 9.2. nvcc 13.2 emits '.version 9.2' for -arch=sm_87 and also for -arch=compute_75 and the no-arch default (target sm_75). nvcc 13.2 rejects -arch=sm_61, sm_72 and compute_61 ('nvcc fatal : Unsupported gpu architecture'); its arch list starts at compute_75/sm_75. Both ptxas and nvPTXCompiler reject --gpu-name=sm_61 ('Value sm_61 is not defined for option gpu-name'), while the driver JIT still runs .target sm_61 PTX.
findings.evidence: GE/tiny_sm87.ptx head '.version 9.2 / .target sm_87'; 'nvcc --list-gpu-arch' -> 'compute_75 compute_80 compute_86 compute_87 compute_88 compute_89 compute_90 compute_100 compute_110 compute_103 compute_120 compute_121'; GE/nvcc_oldarch.txt: 'P2[nvPTXCompiler]: compile FAIL (3): ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_61' is not defined for option 'gpu-name''
findings.why_risky: get_gpu_sm_arch falls back to "sm_61" (attach/nv_attach_utils.cpp:118-149) when driver detection fails. With any CUDA 13 toolkit that fallback makes nvPTXCompilerCompile fail. Detection works on this board (cc 8.7, so sm_87).

findings.topic: (5) Whether the fatbin carries PTX, by nvcc flags
findings.detail: -arch=sm_87: 2 sm_87 ELF entries + 1 sm_87 PTX (compressed). -gencode=arch=compute_87,code=[sm_87,compute_87]: same, PTX present. -arch=compute_87: PTX only. No -arch (default): sm_75 ELF + compute_75 PTX; on sm_87 it runs through the driver JIT. -gencode arch=compute_87,code=sm_87: NO PTX. -arch=native: sm_87 ELF only, NO PTX. '-arch=sm_87 -code=sm_87' is rejected by nvcc ('Value of -arch option (sm_87) must be a virtual code architecture'). Running cuobjdump --extract-ptx all (bpftime's method, nv_attach_impl.cpp:769-856) on the raw .nv_fatbin blob of the -arch=sm_87 binary decompresses the PTX in 3 ms; the result is '.version 9.2 / .target sm_87'. The first ELF entry in the -arch=sm_87 fatbin contains no kernel symbols; its purpose is unverified.
findings.evidence: GE/fatbin.list.txt (cuobjdump --list-elf --list-ptx per binary), e.g. '[native] ... cuobjdump info : No PTX file found to extract'. GE/extract1/tiny_arch_sm87.1.sm_87.ptx ('Extracting PTX file and ptxas options 1: tiny_arch_sm87.1.sm_87.ptx -arch=sm_87')
findings.why_risky: -arch=native and code=sm_87-only builds are common for Jetson apps. They give bpftime's cuobjdump-based PTX patching nothing to patch. bpftime's examples build with no -arch, which yields compute_75 PTX, and that works.

findings.topic: (6) cudart linkage and which libcuda loads at run time
findings.detail: nvcc's default links cudart statically: maps_static has NEEDED = libstdc++, libgcc_s, libc, ld-linux only. __cudaRegisterFatBinary, __cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd and cudaLaunchKernel are local 't' symbols and absent from .dynsym. With -cudart shared they are imported from libcudart.so.13, resolved to /usr/local/cuda/targets/sbsa-linux/lib/libcudart.so.13.2.86. At run time, from the process's own /proc/self/maps, libcuda is /opt/nvidia/l4t-gpu-libs/nvgpu/libcuda.so.1.1. /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 is a symlink to the same file; the toolkit's lib64/stubs/libcuda.so is not loaded. Also mapped: libnvrm_gpu/mem/sync/host1x, libnvos, libnvcuextend, libnvcucompat, libnvsciipc, /dev/nvgpu/igpu0/ctrl. Shared-cudart processes also map libnvidia-ptxjitcompiler.so.595.78 and libnvidia-nvvm70.so.595.78.
findings.evidence: GE/link.txt ('readelf -d', 'ldd', run output 'map: /opt/nvidia/l4t-gpu-libs/nvgpu/libcuda.so.1.1'); 'nm maps_static | grep cudaRegisterFatBinary' -> '00000000000206e8 t __cudaRegisterFatBinary'; 'nm -D maps_static' shows no cuda symbols
findings.why_risky: bpftime finds its hooks by export: gum_module_find_export_by_name(nullptr, "cudaMalloc" / "cudaMallocManaged" / ...) at attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:395-414 and dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, "__cudaRegisterFatBinary") at :370. Neither sees anything in a default (static cudart) build. The examples use 'nvcc -cudart shared' (e.g. example/gpu/launchlate/Makefile:73), so they are fine; arbitrary apps are not.

findings.topic: (7) LLVM 15 NVPTX
findings.detail: llc-15 (15.0.7) knows CPUs up to sm_86 and PTX features up to ptx75; +ptx78 is 'not a recognized feature'. Default .version by -mcpu: sm_60/sm_61 -> 5.0, sm_75 -> 6.3, sm_80 -> 7.0, sm_86 -> 7.1; sm_86 or sm_61 with +ptx75 -> 7.5. -mcpu=sm_87 prints ''sm_87' is not a recognized processor for this target (ignoring processor)' and emits '.version 3.2 / .target sm_87', which ptxas rejects as-is. Every lower-target output compiles for sm_87 unchanged. If only .target is rewritten to sm_87, only the ptx75 outputs survive. Emulating bpftime's real header handling shows the header problem does not bite. filter_compiled_ptx_for_ebpf_program drops all LLVM .version/.target lines (core.cpp:248-285). The module header comes from the trampoline (8.1) or the first header kept by filter_out_version_headers_ptx (core.cpp:165-186). The direct-run path (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1136-1143), which passes the detected sm_87 into LLVM, therefore produces '.version 8.1 / .target sm_87', which compiled and RAN.
findings.evidence: GE/llc15.help.txt, GE/llc15.out.txt ('llc-15 -mcpu=sm_87 (no -mattr) -> rc=0 hdr=[.version 3.2 .target sm_87 ]'), GE/llc15.ptxas.txt, GE/emul.out.txt ('direct: k_sm_87.ptx -> header ['.version 8.1', '.target sm_87', ...]' and 'direct_llc15_sm87.ptx P2[nvPTXCompiler]: compile OK ... value=42 RAN-OK'). Emulator: GE/emul_headers.py. vm/llvm-jit/src/llvm_jit_context.cpp:896-897 creates the target machine with an empty feature string.
findings.why_risky: Latent. Any path that keeps LLVM's own header (or calls generate_ptx("sm_87") and keeps its output) yields invalid PTX with LLVM 15. Fixes would be to pass +ptx75 with sm_86, or to keep stripping headers. The sm_87 measurements used the llc CLI as a stand-in for the C++ API.

findings.topic: PTX ISA downgrade of app code in the ptxpass path
findings.detail: wrap_ptx_with_trampoline (nv_attach_utils.cpp:19-22) puts the trampoline (.version 8.1 / .target sm_61) in front of the patched app PTX. filter_out_version_headers_ptx keeps only the first header. rewrite_ptx_target (nv_attach_utils.cpp:24-60) changes only .target (to sm_87); .version changes only for sm>=100. So nvcc 13.2 app code (ISA 9.2) is assembled as ISA 8.1. For example/gpu/cuda-counter/vec_add.cu, both the -arch=sm_87 PTX and the default compute_75 PTX compile for sm_87 after this merge.
findings.evidence: GE/emul.out.txt: 'ptxpass: vec_add_sm87.ptx -> header ['.version 8.1', '.target sm_87', '.address_size 64'] / ptxas sm_87 rc=0'; nvPTXCompiler compile OK, elf=48704B, load OK
findings.why_risky: Untested for app kernels that use PTX features newer than 8.1; such kernels would fail to assemble after the merge. Applies on any GPU, not only Jetson.

findings.topic: Toolkit layout vs bpftime's cmake/cuda.cmake
findings.detail: CUDA 13.2 here is the unified Arm (sbsa) layout. /usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets contains only sbsa-linux; lib64 links to targets/sbsa-linux/lib and include to targets/sbsa-linux/include. cmake/cuda.cmake:7-8 selects CUDA_TARGET_ARCH=aarch64-linux, so CUDA_LIBRARY_PATH (line 16) and CUDA_INCLUDE_PATH (line 45) point at directories that do not exist. /usr/local/cuda-13.2/extras/CUPTI has only doc/ and samples/, so the include and lib64 paths at cuda.cmake:41-44 and 50-51 are missing. cupti.h and libcupti_static.a live under targets/sbsa-linux/{include,lib}. libnvptxcompiler_static.a (95943050 B) is at /usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets/sbsa-linux/lib, and the lib64 fallback in cuda.cmake:59-60 would find it. nvcc and cuobjdump are not on PATH. bpftime's find_cuobjdump scans /usr/local/cuda* (nv_attach_impl.cpp:707-766) and will find them; Makefiles that call a bare 'nvcc' will not. ld.so.conf includes /usr/local/cuda/targets/sbsa-linux/lib and /opt/nvidia/l4t-gpu-libs/nvgpu.
findings.evidence: 'ls /usr/local/cuda-13.2/targets' -> 'sbsa-linux'; 'ls -la /usr/local/cuda-13.2' -> 'lib64 -> targets/sbsa-linux/lib'; 'ls /usr/local/cuda-13.2/extras/CUPTI/lib64' -> 'No such file or directory'; 'which cuobjdump nvcc' -> 'cuobjdump not found / nvcc not found'
findings.why_risky: Likely to break or misconfigure the first -DBPFTIME_ENABLE_CUDA_ATTACH=ON build (missing include and lib paths, CUPTI lookup) unless the paths are overridden. That is the build agent's area; reported here as environment facts.

findings.topic: concurrentManagedAccess=0
findings.detail: The CPU must not touch managed memory while any kernel is running on this device. bpftime only hooks cudaMallocManaged (attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:400-405) and makes no managed allocations of its own. A grep of runtime/ and attach/ for MallocManaged, cuMemAllocManaged and cudaMemAttach found nothing else.
findings.evidence: GE/attrs.out.txt 'cudaDevAttrConcurrentManagedAccess = 0'; grep output (only the hook and the enum in nv_attach_impl.hpp:64)
findings.why_risky: Only matters if a host-side helper reads or writes a target app's managed buffers while its kernels run.

findings.topic: (8) nvgpu restrictions visible to a normal user
findings.detail: dmesg_restrict=1, so I used journalctl -k (user is in group adm). During these tests the only nvgpu messages came from my deliberate host-pointer fault ('sm machine check err', 'error notifier set to 13 ... owned by hostreg', plus a channel dump). There was also 'Error reporting is not supported in this platform'. No messages about pinning, nvmap or registration limits. An older entry from 11-06 is a similar fault by process 'mem' (an earlier lesson demo). sysfs: railgate_enable=0, is_railgated=no, tpc_fs_mask=0xf0, gpc_fs_mask=2, tsg_timeslice_max_us=50000, tsg_timeslice_min_us=1000, ptimer_ref_freq=31250000, GPU devfreq cur 1020000000. Xorg and gnome-shell hold GPU channels. /sys/module/nvgpu/parameters/* returns 'Permission denied'. CPU5 was at 1728000 (jetson_clocks on).
findings.evidence: GE/journal.txt; 'journalctl -k --since 2026-11-09 01:30' (154 lines, all from the hostptr fault at 01:44:03); sysfs reads of /sys/devices/platform/bus@0/17000000.gpu/*
findings.why_risky: Nothing restrictive found. A faulting GPU program shows up as an SM machine check in the kernel log, which helps debugging.

findings.topic: Kernel BPF array map mmap + cuMemHostRegister: unverified
findings.detail: array_map_kernel_gpu.cpp:288-302 registers the mmap of a kernel BPF_F_MMAPABLE array map, not /dev/shm. I did not test this because creating the map needs CAP_BPF (unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1) and I did not use sudo. A ready probe is built: GE/kmap.cu and GE/kmap. It creates the map, mmaps it, calls cuMemHostRegister(PORTABLE|DEVICEMAP), has a kernel fill it, and checks the values through BPF_MAP_LOOKUP_ELEM. Run unprivileged, it exits cleanly with EPERM.

readers.summary: This area covers what upstream bpftime, the papers about it, and NVIDIA's CUDA 13 and Tegra docs say about bpftime's CUDA attach (attach/nv_attach_impl, runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu, example/gpu) running on this Orin board (sm_87, nvgpu, JetPack 7.2.1 = L4T 39.2.1 with CUDA 13.2.2). Upstream has made no GPU changes since our base: official/master 25e250d6 is 3 commits ahead of 177a1dc and none of them touch GPU paths. Everything still to come is in unmerged PRs. Upstream develops and tests GPU support only on x86_64 discrete GPUs with CUDA 12.x: the CI runs on a self-hosted X64 runner, the docs say "CUDA 12.x recommended / experimental", and the papers were evaluated on a P40 and an RTX 5090. Nobody upstream has reported running it on a Jetson; the only Orin user (DeepRoute, Orin X, CUDA 11.4/12.1) has an unmerged memory-ordering fix (PR #503). I checked the main CUDA 13 risk on this board with static analysis plus gdb. CUDA 13.0+ nvcc host stubs call __cudaGetKernel and then __cudaLaunchKernel(cudaKernel_t). In libcudart 13.2, __cudaLaunchKernel tail-branches into cudaLaunchKernel, so cudaLaunchKernel receives a heap kernel handle instead of the host-stub address. bpftime looks kernels up by the host-stub address, so its main lookup will miss for every app built here. This matches the open upstream issue #646 (GB300, aarch64, CUDA 13.2: probes never fire, "resolved _fini"). Its driver-level cuLaunchKernel hook might still rescue launches, because the exported cuLaunchKernel is reached here (gdb), but that is not verified. Orin-specific problems: (a) CUDA memory IPC is not supported here (cuIpcGetMemHandle returns CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED, verified). GPU_ARRAY, PERGPUTD_ARRAY and GPU_HASH maps therefore throw when created, which knocks out 9 of the 15 upstream CI examples. (b) Registering host memory works: cudaHostRegister on a MAP_SHARED /dev/shm segment succeeds and GPU writes are visible to the CPU (verified). That means HOST maps, the GPU ringbuf, CPU maps through helper calls and the kernel-shared map should be usable. (c) Pageable malloc memory faults on the GPU (verified). Build: cmake/cuda.cmake expects targets/aarch64-linux, but CUDA 13.2 here only installs targets/sbsa-linux (PR #647 hit the same thing). Configuring therefore needs a symlinked shim CUDA root. LLVM 15 does not know sm_87; this only affects the direct-run path and probably only causes warnings. llvm-16-dev, which knows sm_87, is installed. Bottom line: a build looks feasible with the shim. Device-side probes on CUDA-13-built apps may silently not fire until bpftime resolves cudaKernel_t handles, and IPC-backed maps cannot work on Orin. Evidence files are in /tmp/claude-2002/-home-jetson-src/6ac0883f-4479-466c-bec5-5fa31cffe4de/scratchpad/gpu-env: probe.out, probe.cu, launch.cu, k.cu, notes.txt, local_patch_stack.diff, and the issue_*.txt / pr_*.txt dumps.

findings.topic: CMake CUDA layout: CUDA 13 on JetPack 7.x installs targets/sbsa-linux, but bpftime looks for targets/aarch64-linux
findings.detail: cmake/cuda.cmake:11 maps aarch64 to CUDA_TARGET_ARCH=aarch64-linux. Lines 19 (CUDA_LIBRARY_PATH incl. lib/stubs) and 45 (CUDA_INCLUDE_PATH) are built from it. Only the nvptxcompiler find_library (line 59) has a ${ROOT}/lib64 fallback that works. extras/CUPTI holds only doc/ and samples/, so line 50 falls back to the dynamic 'cupti' library (libcupti.so is in sbsa-linux/lib), and the CUPTI include fallback at lines 41-43 points at missing directories (cupti*.h are in include/). PR #647's author hit the same problem on GB300 and worked around it with a symlink; there is no upstream fix. NVIDIA: 'With JetPack 7 series, Jetson software aligns with the Server Base System Architecture (SBSA)'. I have not run a configure, so the failure mode is unverified; a missing cuda.h at compile time is the expected one.

findings.topic: CUDA 13 launch ABI: cudaLaunchKernel gets a cudaKernel_t handle while bpftime keys kernels by host-stub address (likely root cause of upstream #646)
findings.detail: In CUDA 13.x headers without __NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH, nvcc host stubs do `static cudaKernel_t __handle; __cudaGetKernel(&__handle, fun)` and then `__cudaLaunchKernel_helper(__handle, ...)`. The CUPTI CBIDs are suffixed _v13000, so these are new in 13.0. In libcudart.so.13 (sbsa), __cudaLaunchKernel is a thunk ending in `b cudaLaunchKernel`. Checked at runtime with gdb on this board: for a <<<>>> launch, cudaLaunchKernel's x0 (func) equals the cudaGetKernel handle (a heap address), not the host stub. bpftime records hostFun (arg 1 of __cudaRegisterFunction) in symbol_address_to_fatbin and looks up `func` there, so the main lookup misses for every kernel compiled with CUDA >=13. It then takes the late-attach fallback, which resolves the handle with dladdr and the ELF symbol cache; zero-size symbols have no end check there, so the result can be a wrong name such as `_fini`. This is the exact symptom of upstream issue #646 (GB300 Grace aarch64, CUDA 13.2, driver 595.71.05, LLVM 18): 'Late attach launch: resolved _fini but no patched CUfunction is registered'. The original kernel runs and the probe never fires. The issue has been open since 2026-08-14 with no PR; a maintainer says it 'still needs a focused fix/reproducer'. A second path exists: gdb shows libcudart 13.2 does call the exported cuLaunchKernel in /opt/nvidia/l4t-gpu-libs/nvgpu/libcuda.so.1. bpftime's cuLaunchKernel hook swaps in the patched CUfunction by cuFuncGetName name once late bootstrap is done. On GB300 that did not make the probe fire, for an unknown reason. There is no app-side workaround: nvcc 13.2 with -D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH fails to compile ('__cudaLaunchKernel_helper was not declared'). A fix inside bpftime looks feasible: resolve CUkernel names via the cuKernelGetName helper that already exists for graphs, or hook __cudaGetKernel. The cause is not aarch64-specific (any CUDA>=13 app); upstream CI victims use CUDA 12.x. Not yet reproduced end to end with a bpftime build here.

Device-side probes may silently not run, with the original kernel launched instead. Whether the cuLaunchKernel fallback rescues this is unverified, and it failed on the closest reported platform.

findings.topic: CUDA memory IPC is unsupported on Orin (nvgpu), so IPC-backed GPU maps fail at creation
findings.detail: NVIDIA CUDA for Tegra app note (13.5 revision): memory-sharing CUDA IPC APIs are supported only 'on Tegra platforms with open-source GPU driver' starting with CUDA 13.0 (Thor); other Tegra parts should use EGLStream/NvSci/cuMemExportToShareableHandle. Verified on this board: cuIpcGetMemHandle -> CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED. bpftime's GPU_ARRAY_MAP (nv_gpu_shared_array_map) and PERGPUTD_ARRAY_MAP (nv_gpu_per_thread_array_map) call cuMemAlloc and then cuIpcGetMemHandle in their constructors and throw on failure. GPU_HASH_MAP wraps the shared array map. Of the 15 upstream GPU CI examples, 9 use these maps: atomizer, gpu_shared_map, threadscheduling_dynamic_hook, directly_run_on_gpu, kernelretsnoop, threadhist, launchlate, launchlate-kernel-gpu-shared-map, mem_trace; cutlass/faiss/llama/pytorch tests too. The 6 that do not: cuda-counter, cudagraph and threadscheduling (CPU HASH maps via host helper calls), kernel_trace (GPU_RINGBUF over the registered host shm), threadhist-gpu-kernel-shared-map (cuMemHostRegister of a kernel map mmap), and host_map_test (*_HOST_MAP). Upstream knows this: bpftime_shm.hpp comments read 'cuMemAlloc + CUDA IPC (for x86 with IPC support)' vs 'boost::interprocess + cudaHostRegister (for Tegra/platforms without IPC)', and PR #522 added the HOST maps 'for Tegra platforms without CUDA IPC'. Possible fix: this board reports posixFdHandleSupported=1 and vmmSupported=1, so cuMemCreate plus cuMemExportToShareableHandle(POSIX FD) is available. No upstream issue tracks it.

findings.topic: The only sm_87 report upstream, PR #503 (open): memory-ordering fixes for Orin are missing from our tree
findings.detail: dr-xjx (DeepRoute) tested on NVIDIA Orin X (CC 8.7, 12x Cortex-A78AE, CUDA driver/runtime 12.1/11.4) and reported CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (700) and GPU<->CPU synchronization problems running example/gpu/cuda-counter. The original root cause was GPU access to a malloc'd CommSharedMem. That part is likely moot now, because #507 places CommSharedMem in the cudaHostRegister'ed shm segment (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:386-421). The current PR head adds: volatile flag1/flag2/request_id/map_id in CommSharedMem on both host and trampoline side; ld.volatile.global for the flag2 spin; std::atomic_thread_fence(acquire) in the CUDA watcher thread; cudaHostRegisterMapped|cudaHostRegisterPortable; and GPU_HELPER_MAX_BUF 1<<24 -> 1<<20. Maintainers asked for it to be split and for perf data, then said 'testing locally' (2025-11-27); it was last updated 2026-08-09 and is unmerged. None of these changes are in our tree. Whether they are needed on CUDA 13.2 / L4T 39 is unverified. The same author's syscall-server race fix #563 was 'Verified on AArch64 (NVIDIA Orin)' and merged; they also wrote #498 (aarch64 CUDA path) and #522 (Tegra HOST maps).

findings.topic: Upstream and literature claim no Jetson/aarch64 device-side validation
findings.detail: Docs (eunomia.dev 'Write and Run eBPF on GPU with bpftime', last updated 2026-05-21) say 'GPU support is still experimental', 'NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit (12.x recommended)', 'LLVM 15+' and give -DBPFTIME_CUDA_ROOT=/usr/local/cuda-12.6 as the example. They do not mention aarch64, Jetson or iGPUs. The in-tree README lists 'Currently only supports specific CUDA version formats'. The GPU CI runs only on [self-hosted, Linux, X64, gpu] with CUDA 12.x: gpu-examples probes /usr/local/cuda then 12.9..11.8, and ptxpass uses CUDA 12.6 + LLVM 18. Papers: eGPU (HCDS'25) was evaluated on an NVIDIA P40 with dual Xeon E5-2697v2. gpu_ext (arXiv 2512.12615v2, 2025-12-20) used an RTX 5090 (Core Ultra 9 285K) and a P40, and its driver half 'extends the NVIDIA Open GPU Kernel Modules' UVM, which does not apply to Orin's nvgpu. The LPC 2025 talk claims '3-10x faster than NVBit' without naming a platform. Hardware seen in issues/PRs: L4 sm_89 x86 CUDA 12.8 (#695, #708, #709); RTX 5090 CUDA 12.9 (#552); sm_61/sm_120 (#528); GB300 aarch64 CUDA 13.2 (#645 fixed by #647; #646 open); GB200 ARM64 CUDA 13 host-side uprobes only (#720, open, no device-side injection); Orin X CUDA 11.4/12.1 (#503 open, #563 merged). findings.topic: nvcc 13.2 defaults: sm_75 + PTX 9.2, static cudart, hidden __global__ symbols
findings.detail: Without -arch, nvcc 13.2 embeds an sm_75 cubin plus compute_75 PTX with `.version 9.2`. bpftime rewrites .target to the detected sm_87 and keeps .version when sm<100. When a probe patches a module, the merged PTX takes the trampoline's `.version 8.1` header (wrap_ptx_with_trampoline + filter_out_version_headers_ptx keeps the first header); whether CUDA-13-generated PTX bodies ever need features newer than 8.1 is unverified. nvcc's default is --cudart static, and bpftime finds hook targets only through exported symbols (gum_module_find_export_by_name(nullptr, ...)); upstream examples therefore build victims with `nvcc -cudart shared`. CUDA 13.0 also gives __global__ stubs and __device__/__constant__ variables hidden ELF visibility by default; NVIDIA says --device-entity-has-hidden-visibility=false restores the old behaviour. bpftime's name fallback also reads .symtab, so this only hurts stripped binaries (e.g. the device-global mirroring fallbacks).

findings.topic: Host-registered shared memory works on this board (positive result)
findings.detail: bpftime's agent cudaHostRegister's the whole boost shm segment (#507) and reaches CommSharedMem, HOST maps and the ringbuf through cudaHostGetDevicePointer / cuMemHostGetDevicePointer. NVIDIA: cudaHostRegister 'is supported only on I/O coherent devices that have a non-zero value for' cudaDevAttrHostRegisterSupported, which on Tegra means CC>=7.2, and on SoC iGPUs 'the memory range is page-locked'. Verified here: hostRegisterSupported=1; cudaHostRegister(cudaHostRegisterMapped) on a 2 MiB MAP_SHARED /dev/shm mapping succeeds; the device pointer differs from the host pointer (canUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem=0, so bpftime is right to use GetDevicePointer); a kernel write through it is visible to the CPU (41->42). Pageable malloc memory faults on the GPU (cudaErrorIllegalAddress; pageableMemoryAccess=0 because GPU access to pageable memory is 'only possible from Thor SoC onwards'). concurrentManagedAccess=0, so cudaMemPrefetchAsync is unsupported; that only affects open PR #526. P2P and RDMA are unsupported on Tegra, so GDRCopy (#536, opt-in BPFTIME_ENABLE_GDRCOPY) does not apply.

findings.topic: LLVM 15 NVPTX backend has no sm_87
findings.detail: llc-15 lists processors up to sm_86 and PTX features up to ptx75. With -mcpu=sm_87 it prints "'sm_87' is not a recognized processor for this target (ignoring processor)" and emits `.version 3.2 .target sm_87`. bpftime passes the detected arch to LLVM only in the direct-run path; the kprobe/kretprobe/memcapture passes use LLVM target sm_61. Both strip LLVM's headers and use the trampoline's .version 8.1 with the rewritten target, and createNVPTXTargetMachine does not validate the CPU. The expected effect is warnings plus generic codegen, not failure (unverified). llvm-16-dev is installed (/usr/lib/llvm-16/lib/cmake/llvm/LLVMConfig.cmake) and llc-16 emits `.version 7.4 .target sm_87`. llvm-17/18-dev are not installed (apt candidates exist). Upstream ptxpass CI uses LLVM 18.

findings.topic: CUDA 13 API and architecture removals vs bpftime
findings.detail: CUDA 13.0 removed offline compilation for Maxwell, Pascal and Volta; nvcc 13.2 here supports sm_75..sm_121, including sm_87/compute_87. bpftime falls back to 'sm_61' only if SM auto-detection fails, which nvPTXCompiler 13.x would reject. synthesis.verdict:
Plausible, but not out of the box. What has been shown on this Orin: the GPU half works in a replica. bpftime's PTX rewrite (trampoline plus an LLVM-15 probe, .version 8.1 / .target sm_87) compiled with nvPTXCompiler 13.2 for sm_87, loaded, ran, and wrote 1024/1024 probe hits and a globaltimer value into a host-registered map (gpu-env/attach-probe/mini_pipeline.sm87.txt:39). cudaHostRegister of /dev/shm, the iGPU<->CPU helper-call handshake and GPU atomics on host memory also all work (board report).

Three confirmed problems stand between that and a working probe:
(1) Build. cmake/cuda.cmake only knows targets/aarch64-linux, while CUDA 13.2 here installs targets/sbsa-linux. A symlink alias root fixes configure and syntax-only compiles. No real compile or link has been done.
(2) Launch redirection. nvcc 13.2 default builds launch through a cudaKernel_t/CUkernel handle. bpftime cannot name that handle on either hook path: cuFuncGetName returns 400 on it, and cuKernelGetName, which returns the right name, is never tried. So the unpatched kernel runs and nothing reports an error. This is shown by source plus a gdb trace, not yet end to end. Victims built with -D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH -Xcompiler -D__NV_LEGACY_LAUNCH (verified here to build, import cudaLaunchKernel and run) should be redirected through the late-attach name path.
(3) Maps. CUDA IPC is unsupported on this nvgpu iGPU (error 801), so map types 1501/1502/1503 cannot be created. Only the 1512/1513 HOST maps, the 1527 ringbuf and CPU maps reached through host calls are usable. That leaves 6 IPC-free examples plus 2 that need root.

Biggest unknown: whether the first CUDA-ON aarch64 build links and its runtime chain fires inside a victim. That chain is: libnvptxcompiler_static.a linked into a .so, three static-LLVM pass .so files loaded with dlmopen, Frida inline hooks on libcudart.so.13 and the L4T libcuda.so.1, and the cuobjdump-based late bootstrap. None of it has ever run here, and unlike the launch-ABI gap it has no verified workaround. Plan steps 4-7 (build, then kernelretsnoop with a legacy-launch vec_add) answer it.
synthesis.architecture_summary:
Two processes share one boost::interprocess segment, /dev/shm/<BPFTIME_GLOBAL_SHM_NAME> (default 128 MiB).

(a) Loader side. A libbpf app runs with LD_PRELOAD=libbpftime-syscall-server.so. Its programs are SEC("kprobe/<mangled kernel>") or kretprobe and use GPU helper ids 501-511.
- The server intercepts bpf() and perf_event_open and creates maps and programs in the segment.
- In a CUDA build it also constructs cuda_comm_shared_mem, a CommSharedMem holding flag1/flag2, a request union and a response union. It is about 2 MiB with GPU_HELPER_MAX_BUF=1<<20 (runtime/src/bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1072-1084, runtime/include/bpf_attach_ctx.hpp:43,93-102).
- GPU maps 1501/1502/1503 are cuMemAlloc'd by the server and exported with cuIpcGetMemHandle (nv_gpu_shared_array_map.cpp:42-63).
- The 1527 ringbuf and the 1512/1513 HOST maps live in plain shm.

(b) Victim side. A CUDA app linked with shared cudart runs with LD_PRELOAD=libbpftime-agent.so.
- The agent overrides __libc_start_main and runs bpftime_agent_main from the replaced main (agent.cpp:561-582). That is after the app's ELF constructors, so __cudaRegisterFatBinary has already run.
- It opens the segment, cudaHostRegister's the whole of it, and gets device addresses from cudaHostGetDevicePointer / cuMemHostGetDevicePointer. This is required on Orin, where canUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem=0.
- A watcher thread polls CommSharedMem every 1 ms and serves GPU->host helper calls: CPU-map ops, printk, pid (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:111-279).
- nv_attach_impl uses Frida-gum to replace, in libcudart.so.13: cudaLaunchKernel(_ptsz), the __cudaRegister* functions and the memcpy-symbol functions; and in libcuda.so.1: cuLaunchKernel and cuGraph*KernelNode*.
- It loads three ptxpass .so files (kprobe_entry, kretprobe, memcapture, each with static LLVM 15) via dlmopen(LM_ID_NEWLM), plus an nvPTXCompiler wrapper .so. Their paths are baked into the build dir (DEFAULT_PTX_PASS_EXECUTABLE, attach/nv_attach_impl/CMakeLists.txt:72; override with BPFTIME_PTXPASS_LIBRARIES).

Late bootstrap. When a CUDA attach is created it runs synchronously in the agent-init thread (nv_attach_impl.cpp:228, 1953-1981):
1. Scan the loaded ELF modules for .nv_fatbin and .nvFatBinSegment.
2. Run cuobjdump --extract-ptx through posix_spawn with LD_PRELOAD cleared. Only PTX can be patched; a SASS-only fatbin yields nothing.
3. Each pass compiles the eBPF program to PTX with LLVM NVPTX at sm_61, strips LLVM's headers, and injects calls at kernel entry, at ret, or at ld/st.
4. Prepend the trampoline PTX (helpers, map access, host-call spin protocol; .version 8.1). Keep only the first header and rewrite .target to the detected SM: BPFTIME_SM_ARCH, else the cuDevice attribute (sm_87 here), with an sm_61 fallback.
5. Compile with nvPTXCompiler --gpu-name=sm_87 -O3 inside a Boost thread pool. An exception there ends in std::terminate.
6. cuModuleLoadDataEx into the primary context, then copy constData (the CommSharedMem device pointer) and map_info (map types and device pointers).
7. Prefill a table from kernel name to patched CUfunction (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1677-1748; nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:103-280).

Launch redirection.
- The cudaLaunchKernel replacement first looks in a host-stub-keyed map. That map is filled only if the registration hooks saw the fatbin, which never happens for the main executable in preload mode.
- It then resolves the host-stub address to a symbol name (dladdr, then .symtab) and calls cuLaunchKernel on the patched function (nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:165-245).
- The cuLaunchKernel replacement names the CUfunction with cuFuncGetName and swaps in the patched one (frida_setup.cpp:489-527).
- nvcc 13.2 default stubs call __cudaGetKernel and then __cudaLaunchKernel, so cudaLaunchKernel receives a heap handle and cuLaunchKernel receives a CUkernel. Both lookups miss.

Device side. Probe code reads and writes maps 1502/1503/1504/1512/1513 directly through device pointers in map_info, and writes the 1527 ringbuf into registered shm. All other maps go through the flag1/flag2 host-call protocol (membar.sys + spin on the GPU side). The loader reads results straight from shm (ringbuf polling, map dumps).

Paths written as gpu-env/... mean /tmp/claude-2002/-home-jetson-src/6ac0883f-4479-466c-bec5-5fa31cffe4de/scratchpad/gpu-env (session scratch, may disappear). Repo paths are relative to /home/jetson/src/bpftime-daily-state/worktrees/177a1dc465ff/candidate.

blockers.title: CUDA 13.2 handle-based launch: kernels built with default nvcc settings run unpatched and nothing reports it
blockers.detail: nvcc 13.2 host stubs call __cudaGetKernel(&h, stub) and then __cudaLaunchKernel(h, ...). libcudart's thunk branches into cudaLaunchKernel with func = h, a heap address; cudart then calls the exported cuLaunchKernel with the same h, which is a CUkernel cast to CUfunction. Each bpftime path misses: (a) symbol_address_to_fatbin is keyed by host stub, and is empty in preload mode anyway. (b) The late path resolves h with dladdr, then the .symtab nearest-symbol cache; a heap address gives nullopt, or a zero-size symbol such as _fini (the symptom in upstream #646). (c) The cuLaunchKernel path tries only the find_original_kernel_name cache, which holds patched CUfunctions only, and cuFuncGetName, which returns 400 on h. The original kernel launches and nothing is logged above DEBUG. The bug is not Jetson-specific, but CUDA 13.2 is the only toolkit on the board. Shown by source plus a gdb trace; not yet run end to end with a bpftime build.

Verified here: rc=0, imports plain cudaLaunchKernel, runs. -D alone fails with '__cudaGetKernel was not declared'. Those victims should take the late path (dladdr/.symtab gives '_Z9vectorAddPKfS0_Pf', then the patched CUfunction). Fix inside bpftime, to check in a later improvement round: in cu_launch_kernel_common, fall back to cuKernelGetName((CUkernel)func) when cuFuncGetName fails, using the existing helper at frida_setup.cpp:473-487; do the same in cuda_launch_kernel_common before resolve_host_function_symbol, or hook __cudaGetKernel to record handle -> host stub/name. Also stop resolve_host_function_symbol from returning zero-size symbols for addresses outside every module. Small upstream PR candidate (relates to #646).

blockers.title: No CUDA IPC on this nvgpu iGPU: map types 1501/1502/1503 fail at creation, which blocks most examples
blockers.detail: cuIpcGetMemHandle returns 801 CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED. GPU_ARRAY_MAP 1503 and PERGPUTD_ARRAY_MAP 1502 call cuMemAlloc + cuIpcGetMemHandle in the syscall server and throw. GPU_HASH_MAP 1501 contains an nv_gpu_shared_array_map_impl, so it fails the same way. The loader then fails to load its skeleton. blockers.title: A victim must carry PTX and link cudart shared
blockers.detail: Only PTX can be patched; a SASS-only fatbin gives 'Got 0 PTX files' and nothing is instrumented. Builds with -arch=native or '-gencode ...code=sm_87' carry no PTX. The nvcc 13.2 default (no -arch) carries compute_75 PTX at .version 9.2. The hooks find their targets by export (dlsym RTLD_NEXT and gum export lookup), but nvcc links cudart statically by default, which leaves __cudaRegisterFatBinary and cudaLaunchKernel as local symbols. cuBLAS ships PTX only for sm_120. The examples and benchmark/gpu/workload meet these rules (-cudart shared, no -arch); many Jetson apps do not.
blockers.evidence: board GE/fatbin.list.txt ('[native] ... No PTX file found to extract'); board GE/link.txt (`nm maps_static` -> 't __cudaRegisterFatBinary'); example/gpu/cuda-counter/Makefile:73 and benchmark/gpu/workload/Makefile:4,13 (-cudart shared, no -arch); attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:346,370 (export lookups), :770-886 (PTX extraction, per the pipeline report); gpu-env/attach-probe/cublas.listptx.txt
blockers.possible_fix: For the first runs use the example and workload victims unchanged. Before attaching to any other app, check that `cuobjdump --list-ptx <bin>` lists at least one PTX file and that `nm -D <bin> | grep cudaLaunchKernel` shows an import. Rebuild real apps with -cudart shared and a compute_XX PTX target.

blockers.title: Launch-path diagnostics are compiled out if the build copies the daily config

blockers.title: Hook and loader machinery untested on aarch64: Frida inline hooks on libcudart.so.13 and the L4T libcuda.so.1, and dlmopen of the pass .so files

Each of the three passes is dlmopen'ed into a new link-map namespace with its own libc, libstdc++ and static LLVM, and glibc limits both the number of namespaces and the spare static TLS. The text-segment-transformer (dlmopen) agent would also load libcuda a second time. Upstream x86 CI runs the same code; there is no aarch64 run.
