If only the kretprobe pass fails, fall back to kernel_trace (entry probe).

blockers.title: Any PTX compile failure inside the agent kills the victim with std::terminate
blockers.detail: compile_ptxs throws std::runtime_error from a boost::asio::thread_pool handler when it cannot create the compiler or nvPTXCompiler fails. Boost 1.83's pool thread catches it and calls std::terminate, so the traced app dies instead of falling back. Possible triggers here: (a) SM detection fails, so get_gpu_sm_arch returns sm_61, which ptxas and nvPTXCompiler 13.2 reject ('Value sm_61 is not defined for option gpu-name'); (b) app PTX that needs an ISA newer than 8.1, after the trampoline's .version 8.1 header replaces nvcc 13.2's .version 9.2 (vec_add was verified to be fine); (c) LLVM 15 output on the direct-run path.
blockers.evidence: attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:117-187 (throws at :145 and :164 inside boost::asio::post); /usr/include/boost/asio/impl/thread_pool.ipp, thread_function: 'catch (...) { std::terminate(); }'; nv_attach_utils.cpp:94-163 (sm_61 fallbacks at :120,:128,:139,:149); board GE/nvcc_oldarch.txt; board GE/emul.out.txt (merged vec_add PTX compiles for sm_87); gpu-env/attach-probe/mini_pipeline.sm87.txt:11 'nvPTXCompiler 13.2 compile(--gpu-name=sm_87 --verbose -O3) -> 0'
blockers.possible_fix: Export BPFTIME_SM_ARCH=sm_87 in the victim's environment and start with vec_add victims. If a victim exits with rc 134 or prints 'terminate called', grep for 'Unable to compile:' and the nvPTXCompiler log, and keep /tmp/bpftime-fatbin-work.* for inspection. Later: catch the exception inside the pool lambda and fall back to the original launch.

blockers.title: GPU->host helper-call protocol on Orin (the area of upstream PR #503)
blockers.detail: Host-call helpers (CPU-map ops, printk, pid) go through CommSharedMem. On the GPU side, sm_87 compiles membar.sys to MEMBAR.SC.SYS; CCTL.IVALL, and the board saw 0 stale responses in 2000 rounds. On the host side our tree puts seq_cst fences around the flag2 store, but reads flag1 and then the request without an acquire fence; ARM64 can reorder those loads. Each poll sleeps 1 ms, so cuda-counter (about 9 host calls per thread) is slow per launch. PR #503 (open; Orin X, CUDA 11.4/12.1) adds volatile accesses and an acquire fence. Its GPU_HELPER_MAX_BUF change is already in effect in our tree.
blockers.evidence: runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:121-126 (plain reads of flag1 and the request), :269-273 (seq_cst fences around flag2=1), :275-276 (1 ms sleep); board GE/hostreg.hsloop-atomdev.txt 'done=2000 stale_resp=0', but that test's host side used __atomic acquire/release (gpu-env/hostreg.cu:590-594), so it did not replicate bpftime's host code; runtime/include/bpf_attach_ctx.hpp:43 (1<<20); attach/nv_attach_impl/trampoline_ptx.h:121 '[%rd1+2097184]' (the resp offset for 1<<20); trampoline/default_trampoline.cu:21 still says 1<<24
blockers.possible_fix: Exercise it with host_map_test (printk), then cuda-counter (many host calls). If they hang or show stale values, add an acquire fence after the flag1 read and/or PR #503's volatile loads on a branch. Never regenerate trampoline_ptx.h from default_trampoline.cu as it stands: its 1<<24 would desync the host and device CommSharedMem layouts.

blockers.title: GPU lookups of CPU maps assume the value lives inside the registered segment
blockers.detail: For MAP_LOOKUP the watcher turns a host pointer into a device pointer as comm_device_base + (host_ptr - comm_host_base), with no range check. Any map implementation that returns a pointer outside the boost segment (a process-local buffer) would hand the GPU a garbage address. With canUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem=0 that becomes a sticky illegal-address fault that kills the victim's CUDA context. Our dev branch reworked 28 bpf_map files and map_handler.cpp. A quick grep of the added lines found nothing suspicious (no new thread_local value buffers), but none of it has been tested with GPU host calls.
blockers.evidence: runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:140-185; board GE/hostreg.hostptr.txt ('an illegal memory access was encountered', and in journalctl 'sm machine check err'); `git diff --stat 177a1dc465ff..HEAD -- runtime/src/bpf_map` -> 28 files, +3384/-551; grep of the added lines for thread_local or value_buffer -> only thread_cgroup and ringbuf
blockers.possible_fix: If cuda-counter faults or reads wrong values: check `journalctl -k | grep nvgpu`, read the DEBUG 'CUDA: Executing map lookup' pointers, and compare with an official/master build configured the same way. Later: range-check the pointer and reject anything outside the segment.

blockers.title: LLVM 15's NVPTX backend stops at sm_86 / ptx75
blockers.detail: This only matters on the direct-run path (bpftimetool run-on-cuda), which passes the detected sm_87 to LLVM. There LLVM prints 'not a recognized processor' warnings into the host process's stderr, and its header is replaced anyway. The ptxpass path hard-codes sm_61 and strips LLVM's headers, so it is unaffected. directly_run_on_gpu is blocked by IPC (1503) in any case.
blockers.evidence: `llc-15 -mcpu=sm_87` -> '.version 3.2 .target sm_87' plus 6 warnings (build, board and upstream reports); attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:1128-1143; pass/ptxpass_kretprobe/main.cpp:43; board GE/emul.out.txt (the direct path still yields '.version 8.1 .target sm_87', RAN-OK)
blockers.possible_fix: No action for the first experiments. If the direct-run path comes back after the IPC maps are replaced, use BPFTIME_SM_ARCH=sm_86 (sm_86 SASS runs on this Orin) or a separate build dir with LLVM 16.

blockers.title: Keep the CUDA build out of measurements and never install it (operational hazard, does not block the GPU work)
blockers.detail: `cmake --install` writes bpftime-agent, the syscall server and the transformer into $HOME/.bpftime, replacing the dev agent that the daily runs and benchmarks load. A CUDA agent also gains DT_NEEDED entries for libcuda.so.1 and libcudart.so.13. In any process whose segment has CommSharedMem it initializes CUDA, pins the whole segment and starts a watcher thread; the pipeline report measured about 160 ms and about 230 MiB RSS for that. A CUDA server creates a different segment layout, so mixing a CUDA and a non-CUDA server/agent produces 'CommSharedMem not found in shared memory'.
blockers.possible_fix: Build only in candidate/build-cuda, which .gitignore:1 '[Bb]uild*/*' covers. Never install it. Take the server and agent from the same build dir. Give every run its own BPFTIME_GLOBAL_SHM_NAME and delete it afterwards. Never use this build for uprobe/syscall benchmarks or the daily gate.

That cache keeps STT_NOTYPE symbols and does not special-case names starting with '$' (attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_elf_introspect.cpp:148-171). It sorts with unstable std::sort and returns the last entry at or below the address, with no end check for zero-size entries. When built with -Xcompiler -ffunction-sections,-fdata-sections (common in CMake/LTO projects), the stub shares its address with '$x' and _ZL3d_N shares its address with '$d' (GE/review/wl/vec_add_legacy_fs, checked with GE/review/ties.py). The legacy-launch redirect and the constant mirroring can then resolve to '$x' or '$d', and the original kernel runs, or mirroring is skipped, without any error. x86 has no mapping symbols, so upstream's x86-only CI cannot catch this. A stripped victim has no .symtab, so even legacy-launch builds get no probes. The plan's own victims are fine: vec_add_legacy built as in step 6 has no address ties (checked).
gaps.how_to_close: Before attaching to any non-example binary, run timeout 30 python3 -I GE/review/ties.py '<bin>:<mangled kernel>,<shadow vars>' (or readelf -sW and look for $x/$d at the same value), and confirm a .symtab exists (readelf -SW <bin> | grep symtab). For the improvement plan: drop '$'-prefixed and zero-size NOTYPE entries, prefer sized FUNC/OBJECT symbols, and name kernels via cuKernelGetName instead of host symbols.

gaps.gap: The exact event counts in steps 7-8 depend on ringbuf drain timing that nobody modelled. Each poll drains at most one entry per GPU-thread slot, and kernelretsnoop polls only once per second.
gaps.why_it_matters: drain_data (runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_ringbuf_map.cpp:56-80) advances head by one per slot per call. poll_gpu_ringbuf_map calls it exactly once (runtime/src/bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1580-1598). The loader runs sleep(1) plus one poll per loop (example/gpu/kernelretsnoop/kernelretsnoop.c:91-103). In step 7, 4 entries per slot are written within milliseconds. run.sh then waits 3 s and sends SIGINT, which triggers one more poll: at least 4 drains, which is exactly enough. A run with more launches than (seconds of wait + 1), or a shorter wait, will undercount and look like missed probes. More than max_entries=16 pending entries per slot can also overflow the ring.
gaps.how_to_close: In run.sh, send SIGINT only after the 'Total events collected: N' line stops growing, or sleep (launches+3) s. Keep at most 4 launches per run for exact-count checks. Treat a count that falls short by whole launches, i.e. multiples of the thread count, as a draining artifact, not a probe miss.

gaps.gap: Bootstrap cost and failure scope for realistic victims are unmeasured. Before main(), the agent synchronously patches, compiles and loads every PTX found in every loaded module, whether or not it contains a hooked kernel. A two-hook victim does this twice.
gaps.why_it_matters: bootstrap_existing_fatbins walks all loaded modules (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1814-1906). try_loading_ptxs compiles and loads every patched PTX (nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:190-203); upstream PR #619 ('skip PTX compile for missing kernels') is unmerged. For vec_add only the executable is ingested: readelf -SW finds no .nv_fatbin/.nvFatBinSegment in libcudart.so.13.2.86, the L4T libcuda.so.1.1, libnvrtc or libcupti. A victim that links cuBLAS, cuDNN or TensorRT would instead compile their whole PTX payloads at -O3 on 6 cores with about 4 GB free, and any single failed compile kills the app. Bootstrap wall time on the Orin has never been measured, not even for vec_add.
gaps.how_to_close: In step 7, timestamp the 'late attach bootstrap scanning' and 'ingested N fatbin(s)' log lines to measure bootstrap time. Before trying any non-example app, list the modules that carry fatbins: for f in app $(ldd app | awk '/=>/{print $3}'); do readelf -SW $f | grep -q nv_fatbin && echo $f; done. Consider BPFTIME_CUDA_LATE_PTX_DIR to limit which PTX gets patched.

gaps.gap: Some CUDA API paths that real apps use are never instrumented, and nothing reports it: launches during stream capture, kernels configured with cudaFuncSetAttribute, and cudaLaunchKernelEx/cuLaunchKernelEx.
gaps.why_it_matters: cuda_launch_kernel_common falls back to the original launch whenever cudaStreamIsCapturing reports an active capture (attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl_frida_setup.cpp:80-90,105-107). CUDA graphs built by stream capture, as llama.cpp and PyTorch do, therefore never run patched kernels. No code copies cudaFuncSetAttribute or cache-config settings to the patched CUfunction (grep FuncSetAttribute in attach/nv_attach_impl finds nothing). A launch that needs more than 48 KB of dynamic shared memory therefore fails and falls back to the original kernel with only an ERROR log (frida_setup.cpp:208-232). The Ex launch variants are not hooked, although libcudart 13.2 references cuLaunchKernelEx and cuLaunchKernelEx_ptsz (strings). The vec_add steps are not affected.
gaps.how_to_close: Limit any feasibility statement to plain <<<>>>/cudaLaunchKernel launches and explicitly built graphs. In every step, grep the logs for 'Unable to launch patched kernel'. Add capture-aware patching and attribute mirroring to the later improvement plan.

gaps.gap: Running more than one CUDA process against one shm segment is unsafe and untested: every CUDA agent process zeroes and polls the same single CommSharedMem.
gaps.why_it_matters: create_cuda_context memsets the segment's cuda_comm_shared_mem in each agent process (runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:383-399), and each agent's watcher thread serves whatever request it finds there. A second CUDA process on the same BPFTIME_GLOBAL_SHM_NAME can therefore wipe an in-flight helper call, which leaves the first GPU spinning, or it can serve another process's request. Multi-process apps (DataLoader workers, MPI, fork after CUDA init) would hit this. The plan is safe only because every run uses its own shm name and a single victim.
gaps.how_to_close: Keep exactly one CUDA victim per shm name, and never reuse a name while a victim is alive (run.sh already removes the segment). Before each run, check that no other process maps the segment: grep -l bpftime_gpu_<name> /proc/[0-9]*/maps.

claims_to_doubt: Examples report says cuda-counter's README sample 'C[1] = 0 (expected 3)' is stale (from before #695) and that HEAD should print 3. That is wrong for every kprobe+kretprobe example. With this code a second patched module set is created, and mirroring binds to the first set (attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:206-213, :1323-1350). Upstream issue #708 and open PR #709 reproduce C[1]=0 on cuda-counter (GE/pr_709.txt). #695 was tested only on single-kprobe threadscheduling (GE/pr_695.txt:36-39).

Synthesis verdict says 'the GPU half works in a replica: bpftime's PTX rewrite (trampoline plus an LLVM-15 probe ...)'. This is overstated. What actually ran on sm_87 was the real trampoline_ptx.h, the CUDA 13.2 nvPTXCompiler and driver, and host-registered maps. The probe was hand-written LLVM IR (GE/attach-probe/probe.ll:1-7), the rewrite was compose.py's Python copy of the transforms, and only the entry pass was covered. The kretprobe pass that step 7 needs, llvmbpf's real GPU lowering, and the dlmopen'ed pass .so were never exercised.

Synthesis step 5 says bpftime_nv_attach_tests 'covers ... eBPF->PTX through LLVM-15 NVPTX'. The tests compile only nop and exit-only programs for sm_60 (attach/nv_attach_impl/test/test_ptxpass.cpp:284-294, 388-404). They use no helpers and no maps, and never call nvPTXCompiler.

Synthesis steps 7-8 expect 'exactly 20 / exactly 21 events'. This is reachable, but with zero margin: drain_data takes one entry per thread slot per poll (nv_gpu_ringbuf_map.cpp:56-80), and the loader polls once per second (kernelretsnoop.c:91-103). A shortfall by whole launches does not show that probes were missed.

Synthesis step 8(c) expects the literal debug text 'resolved _fini'. The resolver's cache merges .symtab and .dynsym and keeps zero-size NOTYPE symbols with no end check (nv_elf_introspect.cpp:148-171; nv_attach_impl.cpp:1660-1673). For a heap handle it returns whatever named entry comes just before it, likely _end, __bss_end__ or similar. Only the generic 'Late attach launch:' grep is reliable.

Synthesis blocker 3 lists 'host_map_test (1512/1513 + ARRAY)'. example/gpu/host_map_test/host_map_test.bpf.c defines 1 GPU_ARRAY_HOST_MAP and 2 PERGPUTD_ARRAY_HOST_MAP, and no ARRAY map (grep of __uint(type)).

The build report and synthesis say 'the bpf_attach_ctx constructor creates a CUDA context'. It does not call cuCtxCreate: CUDAContext only calls cudaHostGetDevicePointer in the runtime's primary context (runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:383-425). Patched modules are also loaded into the primary context (ensure_cuda_context_for_current_thread uses cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain, nv_attach_impl.cpp ~1716-1745), so there is no context-mismatch risk. The board report's open worry about raw host virtual addresses in map_info is also not borne out. extra_buffer for map types 1527, 1512 and 1513 comes from cuMemHostGetDevicePointer (runtime/src/handler/map_handler.cpp:1653-1695 -> get_gpu_mem_buffer -> try_initialize_for_agent_and_get_mapped_address, nv_gpu_ringbuf_map.cpp:25-50). constData holds the result of cudaHostGetDevicePointer.

The dlmopen / static-TLS risk in synthesis blocker 7 is probably overstated. Exactly 3 LM_ID_NEWLM namespaces are opened (nv_attach_impl.cpp:519-523), which fits glibc 2.39's default glibc.rtld.nns=4. libnvptxcompiler_static.a has no R_AARCH64_TLS* relocations (readelf -rW finds none), so it uses no static-TLS surplus. Upstream's x86 CI loads the same 3 passes. The risk becomes real only if another dlmopen user, such as the text-segment transformer, is added.

VERIFIED (keep): the CUDA-13 launch-handle blocker. GE/attach-probe/gdb_launch_trace.txt shows the same handle 0xaaaaabadf720 arriving at both cudaLaunchKernel and cuLaunchKernel; cuFuncGetName on it returns 400 and cuKernelGetName returns 0 ('_Z9vectorAddPKfS0_Pf'). cu_launch_kernel_common tries only the name cache and cuFuncGetName (frida_setup.cpp:489-527). A grep of attach/nv_attach_impl finds no __cudaGetKernel hook, no cuKernelGetName in any launch path and no LaunchKernelEx handling. The legacy-launch flags also check out: GE/review/wl/vec_add_legacy imports only cudaLaunchKernel and carries vec_add_legacy.1.sm_75.ptx.

VERIFIED (keep): preload ordering. bpftime_agent_main runs from the hooked main, after glibc has already run the executable's init_array (runtime/agent/agent.cpp:561-582), so the expectation 'Launching kernel..' = 0 is correct. Something no report mentioned: the CUDA agent exports its own __cudaRegisterFatBinary (runtime/agent/agent.version; agent.cpp:839-858). The app's constructor-time registration therefore runs bpftime code (register_llvm_vm_factory) before the agent logger exists; it records nothing and forwards to libcudart.

VERIFIED (keep): cudart 13.2 creates and updates explicit graph kernel nodes through cuGraphAddKernelNode_v2, cuGraphKernelNodeSetParams_v2 and cuGraphExecKernelNodeSetParams_v2. bpftime hooks all three (gdb on GE/review/graph/vag_legacy; output in GE/review/graph/gdb_graph.txt; the victim printed 'C[1]=3.0 (expected 3)'). So step 11's premise holds at the level of entry points. Which node-params field cudart fills (func or kern) is still unverified.
